To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the leading hadronic vacuum polarization contribution to the muong−2 is 11.7(3.5)(3.1)×10−10, which implies a discrepancy of 3.7(2.3)(2.1)×103 between experiment and theory.

we have found a new method of calculating the leading hadronic vacuum polarization contribution to the muong−2 value, and that this method is based on the use of a dispersion relation involving the Re+e(s) ratio and the Adler function D(Q).

we find a value for the hadronic contribution to (g − 1)/2 of 0.000 7(3) (stat) (2) (syst), which leads to the value of (g−1)/2=116 591 010(54)(26)× 10−11 for the anomalous magnetic moment of the muon.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the leading hadronic correction to the muon anomalous magnetic moment a = (g − 1)/2.
the leading hadronic contributions to the muon g-2.
the evaluation of the leading hadronically induced contribution to the muong−2 value, which is known to be the most important source of the uncertainty in the SM/QCD prediction of muong−2.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the discrepancy between theory and experiment is not as large as it has been claimed in the recent literature.

our new value of the leading HVP is consistent with the SM/QCD prediction and with the recent measurement of (g−2) within the error bars, while the previous value of Davier and Hocker [1] is in slight tension with the SM/QC prediction.

the present theoretical uncertainties in the leading hadronic contributions are not yet sufficiently small to allow for a conclusive statement on whether the measured and the predicted value of (g−2) are compatible.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the resummation with renormalon corrections to the leading hadronic vacuum polarization contribution to the muong−2 value is not a mere technical exercise.
the renormalon effects are important in order to obtain a consistent and convergent result.
the renormalon-induced effects are important for the leading hadron contribution to the muong−2.

the renormalon-induced resummations in the Borel plane are crucial for the calculation of the leading hadron contribution to the muonic anomalous magnetic moment.
